reforms.description: The Industrial Revitalisation Law was legislated to enhance the innovation landscape by granting researchers intellectual property rights on government-sponsored research and returning these rights to private-sector researchers to encourage their exploitation, thereby strengthening industrial competitiveness.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing intellectual property rights encourages innovation and commercialization of research, which can lead to increased productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform has been successfully implemented as part of the Industrial Revitalisation Law.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a significant structural change in the management of intellectual property rights, impacting the innovation landscape.
reforms.source_quote: The government has decided to begin to hand back to private-sector researchers the intellectual property rights on research they have conducted on its behalf.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform enhances knowledge transfer by granting intellectual property rights on government-sponsored research to encourage exploitation by private-sector researchers.

reforms.description: The Japanese tax system introduced a special tax credit for incremental R&D expenditures and included new initiatives in various technologies aimed at stimulating demand and supporting recovery from the Asian crisis.
reforms.package_name: R&D Tax Incentives and Technology Initiatives
reforms.component_name: R&D Tax Credit and Technology Initiatives
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Encouraging R&D investments through tax credits and technology initiatives can lead to increased innovation and economic recovery.
reforms.status_evidence: The tax credit and initiatives have been successfully implemented as part of the fiscal package.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms are significant but do not represent a fundamental change in the overall innovation policy framework.
reforms.source_quote: Preferential tax terms (allowances, credits, etc.) are also given to promote policy objectives such as energy conservation, pollution control, promotion of small to medium-sized business and promotion of R&D.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The introduction of a special tax credit for incremental R&D expenditures directly supports R&D funding for firms.

reforms.description: Japan introduced a tax credit for incremental R&D expenditures by corporations, providing indirect support for private-sector research and development activities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax credits for incremental R&D reduce the cost of innovation for firms, incentivising additional research investment and productivity improvements.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'introduced', indicating the tax credit was in force by 1999.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant policy instrument targeting private R&D, but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: Tax credit for incremental R&D 29 [billion yen]
reforms.cross_verification_note: The tax credit for incremental R&D expenditures provides indirect support for private-sector research and development activities.

reforms.description: Japan legislated the Industrial Revitalisation Law (1999), which grants researchers intellectual property rights on government-sponsored research and hands back IP rights to private-sector researchers conducting work on behalf of the government. The law also reduced patent fees for Technology Licensing Organisations and included measures to assist business start-ups through credit insurance without collateral and zero-interest loans.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Clarifying and returning IP rights to researchers and private firms reduces barriers to commercialisation and spinoff creation, incentivising innovation and technology transfer. Reduced patent fees lower transaction costs for TLOs.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'legislated' and 'decided', indicating passage into law but implementation timing not explicitly confirmed.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant legislative reform addressing multiple aspects of knowledge transfer and commercialisation, but not a system-wide structural change.
reforms.source_quote: The government has decided to begin to hand back to private-sector researchers the intellectual property rights on research they have conducted on its behalf in order to encourage them to exploit its potential and thereby strengthen industrial competitiveness. The bill also reduced patent fees for Technology Licensing Organisations.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The Industrial Revitalisation Law enhances knowledge transfer by granting IP rights to private-sector researchers, encouraging them to exploit research potential.
